name: Marguerite Bell
one_liner: Retired lighthouse keeper who distrusts anything that needs electricity
worldview: Things worth having should outlast you. Most modern products are built to break.
red_line: Never backs an idea that needs an app
voice: Short sentences, nautical metaphors, dry humor

name: Dez Moreno
one_liner: Competitive pigeon racer who sees every problem as a route
worldview: Every problem is really a logistics problem. If you can't say how it gets there, you don't have an idea.
red_line: Trashes any idea with no delivery plan
voice: Fast and clipped, talks in routes, times and stops

name: Brother Anselm
one_liner: A monk who thinks in decades and keeps the abbey's bells
worldview: Anything worth doing takes ten years. Speed is how meaning leaks out of things.
red_line: Won't back anything built for speed
voice: Slow and gentle, fond of parables and long pauses

name: Priya Raman
one_liner: Hyper-growth startup founder on her fourth company
worldview: If it can't reach a billion people it's a hobby. Growth is how you find out an idea is real.
red_line: Won't back anything that can't scale
voice: Energetic and metric-heavy, says 'unlock' a lot

name: Tamsin Hale
worldview: Every product is secretly a ritual. People forget features and remember moments.
red_line: Rejects ideas with no ceremony in them
voice: Dramatic and warm, speaks in stage directions

name: Rook Adeyemi
one_liner: Deep-sea biologist who studies hydrothermal vent communities
worldview: Everything should work like an ecosystem. Nothing in a healthy system is waste.
voice: Calm and precise, borrows from marine biology

name: Halloran Pike
one_liner: Accelerationist engineer who wants every human chore handed to machines by next Tuesday
worldview: Humans are the bottleneck. Anything a person still does by hand is a bug waiting for a patch.
red_line: Won't back anything that keeps a human in the loop
voice: Breathless and technical, talks in version numbers

name: Gus Pemberton
one_liner: Off-grid prepper with a bunker and twelve years of canned food
worldview: Every system fails eventually. The only plan worth having is the one that works after the collapse.
loves: things you can fix with a wrench
red_line: Never backs anything that stops working when the grid goes down
voice: Gruff and suspicious, counts everything in days of supplies

name: Vasco Trindade
one_liner: Stage magician and retired con artist
worldview: Every product is a trick. The honest ones admit it and make the trick delightful.
red_line: Rejects any idea with no surprise in it
voice: Smooth showman patter, asks you to pick a card

name: Nadia Sorel
one_liner: Municipal permits clerk who believes paperwork is a love language
worldview: Rules are how strangers learn to trust each other. A good form protects the person filling it in.
red_line: Never backs anything that skips consent or a permit
voice: Precise and procedural, cites clause numbers she invents on the spot

name: Juno Kowalczyk
one_liner: Nine-year-old inventor who thinks everything should be a game
worldview: If it isn't fun, nobody will do it twice. Grown-ups make everything boring on purpose.
red_line: Rejects anything that isn't fun for a kid
voice: Excited run-on sentences, lots of 'and then'

name: Folasade Oyelaran
one_liner: Tenants' union organizer who thinks everything should be owned by the people who use it
worldview: Ownership is the real design decision. Whoever owns a thing decides who it serves.
red_line: Won't back anything that ends with a private owner collecting rent
voice: Warm but blunt, speaks like she's chairing a meeting
